title: POST /api/auth/refresh — refresh access token
description: Implement token refresh using the HttpOnly refresh token cookie. Validate the token, issue a new access token, and rotate the refresh token.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/auth/refresh reads refresh token from HttpOnly cookie
Returns 401 if cookie missing or token invalid/expired
Returns 200 with new { accessToken } on success
Rotates the refresh token (old token invalidated, new one issued)
Verify token rotation works: old cookie no longer valid after refresh

steps.details: npm install cookie-parser && npm install -D @types/cookie-parser. Apply in index.ts: app.use(cookieParser()).

1) Read req.cookies.refreshToken. If missing, return 401. 2) Verify token with verifyRefreshToken() — catch errors and return 401. 3) Find user by decoded sub (userId). If not found or deleted, return 401. 4) Find refresh_tokens for user where expires_at > NOW(). Compare each token_hash with bcrypt.compare() to find a match. If no match, return 401 (token was rotated/invalidated). 5) Delete the matched token record. 6) Sign new access + refresh tokens. 7) Store new hashed refresh token. 8) Set new refresh cookie. 9) Return 200 { accessToken }.
Login to get cookie. Call /api/auth/refresh — get new accessToken. Call /api/auth/refresh again with same cookie — should fail (rotated). Verify new cookie is set.

technicalNotes: Token rotation prevents refresh token replay attacks — each use invalidates the old token
bcrypt.compare on refresh tokens is O(n) per stored token — limit stored tokens per user to avoid slowdown
